docs.title: John Augustus Williams, Life of Elder John Smith (1870)

quotes.text: We saw no reason why we should not be the same family.
It was not a meeting of Elders or Preachers only, but a popular assembly
Honest doubts respecting the doctrine of the others
Some Reformers still looked upon the Christians as Arians
denied the influence of the Spirit
in the same sense that baptism was for the remission of sins
free or restricted communion
To-day the Landgrave is making every effort to unite us, or at least to make us consider each other brethren and members of Christ’s body
But although we object to be brethren, we wish to live at peace and on good terms.
God has but one people on the earth. He has given to them but one Book, and therein exhorts and commands them to be one family.
But an amalgamation of sects is not such a union as Christ prayed for, and God enjoins.
While there is but one faith, there may be ten thousand opinions; and hence, if Christians are ever to be one, they must be one in faith, and not in opinion.
Let us, then, my brethren, be no longer Campbellites or Stoneites
but let us all come to the Bible, and to the Bible alone, as the only book in the world that can give us all the Light we need.
the controversies of the Church sufficiently prove that Christians never can be one in their speculations upon those mysterious and sublime subjects
I have not one objection to the ground laid down by him as the true scriptural basis of union among the people of God; and I am willing to give him, now and here, my hand.
A song arose, and brethren and sisters, with many tearful greetings, ratified and confirmed the union. On Lord’s day, they broke the loaf together
It may be asked, is there no difference of opinion among you? We answer, we do not know, nor are we concerned to know.
Is it not obvious that all lines drawn from the circumference of any circle towards its centre, will meet in the same point?

As all sects forsake their systems, and return to the apostolic gospel and institutions, they will meet in one and the same centre of faith, hope, and love. We devoutly wish to see Papists and Protestants, every sect coming to this centre, and then I trust they will find all those slanderously called ‘Campbellites,’ rejoicing to receive them.

For they believe that no person but a preacher has a right to administer the ordinances—such as the breaking of the loaf &c. and become very much alarmed at the idea of us common folks receiving the name of kings and priests to the Lord
where three are, a church is, albeit they be laics.
The apparent question at issue was: may a group of believers not set in order with a presbytery eat the Lord’s Supper or not?
were only two christians in any place, such as on shipboard
they ought to commemorate the death of Christ on the first day of the week
Is there any thing to be done at the table of the Lord, which any brother, who can give thanks for a crucified Savior, and repeat the words of the institution, cannot do?
‘The administration of ordinances’ is a popish phrase, and ought to be cashiered from the christian vocabulary.
He would not tolerate a disciple in his church to baptize a candidate, nor to ‘administer the Lord’s supper,’ nor to pray over the loaf or the cup.

Not having any person whom they regarded as filling Paul’s outlines of a bishop, they had appointed two senior members, of a very grave deportment, to preside in their meetings. These persons were not competent to labor in the word and teaching; but they were qualified to rule well
He then called upon a brother
to read a section of the evangelical history.
the president called upon a brother to pray in the name of the congregation.
the whole congregation, brethren and sisters, pronounced aloud the final Amen.
he took a small loaf from the table, and in one or two periods gave thanks for it.
each one waiting upon his brother, until all were served.
There was no stiffness, no formality, no pageantry; all was easy, familiar, solemn, cheerful.
He may of right preach, baptize, and dispense the supper, as well as pray for all men, when circumstances demand it.

For you cannot find in the New Testament one instance of the church having authority to ordain elders or bishops or deacons, or to administer baptism or the supper. You will find that the ministry existed before the church
they believe that no person but a preacher has a right to administer the ordinances — such as the breaking of the loaf
When he is absent the church can do nothing. Like a widow forlorn and desolate, she is solitary and silent.
One, of course, leads in giving thanks. This is not officiating, for any disciple can do this. It does not pertain to any office.
An ordained minister, as representative of Christ presiding at the Lord’s Table, serves in Christ’s place as host at the Table.
within Australian Churches of Christ ‘lay presidency’ is almost the norm
we have denied women the opportunity to pass Communion trays because we have described it as a ‘leadership role.’
Nor was a union between the two congregations finally and formally effected till in July, 1835
to state the anomaly as boldly as possible, the movement is at one and the same time Christocentric and bibliocentric.
her only manual was, ‘The Bible.’ And her all comprehensive creed for the binding of the faithful; ‘Jesus Christ is the Son of God.’
Primitive Sufferings,
We determined that we would own no name but Christian
and that we would subscribe to no creed but the Bible
You know, sir, that I owned no creed but the Bible, and that I was ordained with this understanding by the Presbytery.
After we had given up all creeds and taken the Bible, and the Bible alone, as our rule of faith and practice
Behold my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
her only manual was, ‘The Bible.’ And her all comprehensive creed for the binding of the faithful; ‘Jesus Christ is the Son of God.’
Primitive Sufferings
It shows the true creed, and restores it to its native eminence above all other things in the gospel.
By a series of negations, I might exclude every creed in Christendom from its claims to be called the creed of our religion

if any section of the Christian profession offers it in its practical forms as the basis of Christian union, the symbol of confession for the remission of sins, and the element of our perfection in holiness, save our brethren, the author is not aware of it.
We have no authority but the Bible; we wear no name but ‘Christians;’ and we have no creed but Christ.
to state the anomaly as boldly as possible, the movement is at one and the same time Christocentric and bibliocentric.

The brethren of Stone did not join Alexander Campbell as their leader, nor did the brethren of Campbell join Barton W. Stone as their leader; but each, having already taken Jesus the Christ as their only Leader, in love and liberty became one body
